name: Push Up
instructions: Get into a high plank position (hands and toes on the floor, body straight).
Place your hands close together under your chest, forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers.
Keep arms extended, shoulders stacked over wrists, core tight, and back straight

name: dumbell fly
instructions: Lie flat on a bench (flat, incline, or decline) with a dumbbell in each hand.
Extend arms straight above your chest, palms facing each other, slightly bent elbows.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and core engaged.

name: Cable decline fly
instructions: Set the pulleys on a high position (above shoulder level) on a cable machine.
Attach D-handles and grab one in each hand.
Stand in the center with one foot forward for balance, arms slightly bent, palms facing down/inward.
Step slightly forward so there is tension in the cables, chest lifted, core engaged.

name: push ups
instructions: Place your feet on a stable elevated surface (bench, box, or step).
Hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width, arms extended.
Keep body straight from head to heels, core engaged

name: Normal pushups
instructions: Get into a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Arms straight, shoulders stacked over wrists.
Keep body in a straight line from head to heels, core and glutes tight.

name: Dumbell bench press
instructions: Equipment: Flat bench and a pair of dumbbells.
Position: Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Grip: Hold the dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) or a pronated grip (palms facing forward), depending on comfort

name: Dumbell bench press
instructions: Equipment: Flat bench and a pair of dumbbells.
Position: Sit on the bench holding a dumbbell in each hand on your thighs.
Grip: Palms facing forward (pronated grip).
2. Getting Into Position
Lie back carefully: Use your thighs to help lift the dumbbells as you recline on the bench.
Feet: Keep them flat on the floor for stability.
Dumbbell position: Hold dumbbells at chest level, elbows bent around 90°, upper arms roughly parallel to the floor.

name: Dumbell Bend over row
instructions: Equipment: A pair of dumbbells.
Position: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing your torso (neutral grip) or forward (overhand grip).

name: Pull ups
instructions: Equipment: Pull-up bar (sturdy, overhead).
Grip: Hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, palms facing away from you (overhand grip).
2. Starting Position
Hang from the bar: Arms fully extended, legs straight or slightly bent behind you.
Engage your shoulders: Pull your shoulder blades down and back before starting the pull.

name: Dumbell Squats
instructions: Equipment & Setup
Equipment: A pair of dumbbells.
Grip/Position:
By your sides: Hold one dumbbell in each hand, arms straight down.
Goblet style: Hold one dumbbell close to your chest with both hands.
2. Starting Position
Stand tall: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Posture: Chest up, shoulders back, core engaged.
Dumbbell position: Either at sides or in front of chest, depending on chosen style.
3. Execution
Squat down: Push hips back and bend knees, lowering until thighs are roughly parallel to the floor.
Elbows: If holding dumbbell in front (goblet style), keep elbows pointing downward.
Push up: Press through your heels to return to standing position

name: Normal sqauts
instructions: Setup
Feet: Shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out (~15–30°).
Posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders back, core engaged.
2. Starting Position
Arms can be:
Extended forward for balance
Placed on hips
Held together in front of chest
3. Execution
Lower down:
Push your hips back and bend your knees.
Keep chest upright and back straight.
Go down until thighs are at least parallel to the floor (or slightly lower if mobility allows).
Push up:
Press through your heels to return to the starting position.
Keep knees tracking over toes

name: squats using one dumbbell
instructions: Equipment: One dumbbell (moderate weight).
Grip/Position Options:
Goblet style: Hold the dumbbell vertically at chest with both hands, elbows pointing down.
Single-arm racked: Hold dumbbell on one shoulder (like a front squat variation) for added core challenge.
2. Starting Position
Feet: Shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Posture: Chest up, shoulders back, core tight.
Dumbbell: Held securely in chosen position.

name: Barbell front squat
target: Primary: Quadriceps, glutes  Secondary: Hamstrings, calves, core, upper back (to stabilize bar)
instructions: Equipment: Barbell and squat rack.
Grip / Bar Position:
Clean grip: Hands just outside shoulders, bar resting on front deltoids, elbows high.
Cross-arm grip: Arms crossed, hands resting on bar to stabilize it on shoulders (alternative if wrist mobility is limited).
2. Starting Position
Stand tall: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Core engaged: Tighten abs and keep chest up.
Bar position: Front of shoulders, elbows pointing forward and slightly up.
3. Execution
Lower down: Push hips back slightly, bend knees, and squat down while keeping chest upright.
Depth: Lower until thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below, if mobility allows.
Push up: Drive through heels to stand back up, keeping elbows up and chest tall.
4. Breathing
Inhale while lowering down.
Exhale while driving back up.

name: leg extension
target: primarily target the quadriceps (front of the thighs)
instructions: Equipment & Setup
Equipment: Leg extension machine.
Seat adjustment:
Backrest should support your lower back.
Knees should align with the machine’s pivot point.
Footpad: Position it just above your ankles.
Weight: Select a manageable weight that allows controlled movement.
2. Starting Position
Sit on the machine: Back flat against the seat, feet under the footpad.
Grip handles: Hold the side handles for stability.
Legs: Knees bent at ~90°, feet flexed naturally.
3. Execution
Extend legs: Straighten your knees to lift the footpad, contracting your quadriceps.
Pause: Hold for 1–2 seconds at the top for maximum contraction.
Lower slowly: Slowly bend knees back to the starting position, keeping tension on the quads.

name: Leg press
instructions: Equipment & Setup
Equipment: Leg press machine.
Seat adjustment: Adjust so that when your feet are on the platform, knees are bent at ~90°.
Foot placement: Feet shoulder-width apart on the platform; toes slightly pointed out.
Weight: Choose a manageable weight that allows controlled movement.
2. Starting Position
Sit on the machine: Back flat against the seat, head and shoulders supported.
Foot position: Platform under feet, knees bent.
Grip handles: Hold handles on the sides for stability.
3. Execution
Push platform: Press through your heels to straighten your legs, keeping a slight bend in the knees at the top.
Lower platform: Slowly bend your knees and return to starting position, controlling the movement.
Knee alignment: Keep knees in line with your toes; don’t let them collapse inward or flare outward.

name: machine hack squat
target: quadriceps while providing support for the back
instructions: Equipment & Setup
Equipment: Hack squat machine.
Foot placement: Shoulder-width apart on the platform, toes slightly pointed out.
Back support: Keep back and shoulders against the pad.
Weight: Select a manageable load that allows controlled movement.
2. Starting Position
Position yourself: Stand on the platform, shoulders under pads, back pressed against the support.
Feet placement: Platform under feet, knees slightly bent.
Grip handles: Hold the side handles for stability.
3. Execution
Lower down: Slowly bend knees and hips, keeping your back against the pad. Lower until thighs are roughly parallel to the platform (or slightly deeper if comfortable).
Push up: Press through your heels to return to the starting position. Keep knees in line with toes throughout.
Control: Avoid locking out knees at the top
